title: Two voltages that add to more than the source
story: A 1 V, 1 kHz sine drives a 1 kOhm resistor in series with a capacitor. Choose the capacitor so that, at 1 kHz, the capacitor gets about 0.71 of the source voltage (between -3.5 dB and -2.5 dB) and lags it by roughly 45 degrees. Then the resistor gets about 0.71 V too: the two add to more than 1 V, because they add as arrows.

goals.label: capacitor voltage between -3.5 dB and -2.5 dB of the source at 1 kHz
capacitor voltage lags the source by 40 to 50 degrees at 1 kHz

hints: The capacitor's share is 1 / (1 + j omega R C). Its size is 0.707 (-3 dB) when omega R C = 1.
At 1 kHz, omega = 6283 rad/s. With R = 1000 ohm you need C close to 1 / (6283 x 1000) = 159 nF.
